title: Deburr links its edge runs with a diagonal rapid straight from cutting depth through the part
body:
Deburr leaves every edge run except the last with one diagonal rapid, straight from cutting depth to the next run's start at the clearance plane. The cone is still engaged in the edge it just broke when it rapids up and across the part.

### Measured (main 8f30bee)

The brick from `operations.rs`'s deburr test (`cube((-20,-10,0), (20,10,10))`), stock = the brick, `CM-0600-90`, width 2, window z 6..8. The first moves:

`
move 1: Plunge (-20,-10,25) -> (-20,-10, 8)
move 2: Feed   (-20,-10, 8) -> ( 20,-10, 8)    breaks the front rim
move 3: Rapid  ( 20,-10, 8) -> (-20, 10,25)    <- from cutting depth, diagonally across the part
move 4: Plunge (-20, 10,25) -> (-20, 10, 6)
`

- Generator verify: `RapidInStock` at moves 3, 8 and 13, one per link, so the post is blocked.
- Program sim: the deepest gouge columns (worst 3.80 mm at the (20, -10) corner) sit along those links, deeper than the 2 mm break itself. (The break being charged as a gouge at all is #303.)

### Cause

`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr.rs`, the run loop (lines 235-247): each run opens with `Rapid` to `(first.x, first.y, clearance_z)` from wherever the previous run ended. The vertical retract to clearance is only pushed once, after the last run (lines 248-253).

### Fix

Leave each run straight up to the clearance plane before the traverse, the same move the path already ends with. Pin: every rapid that starts below the clearance plane is vertical, and the brick's deburr verifies with no `RapidInStock`.

**Root cause (confirmed):** `finishing3d/deburr.rs`'s run loop pushes the traverse rapid without a retract first. Measured on the brick: move 3 is `Rapid (20,-10,8) -> (-20,10,25)`, and verify flags `RapidInStock` at 3, 8 and 13.

Suggested labels (I can't set them): `bug`, `P1`, `area:3d`, `source:agent`.
